avoid: Extended entries (price well above EMA-20 at entry) -- CONFIRMED LOSER historically (META Jul 15 at ~8.5% above EMA-20, stopped -8.04% Jul 23). LIVE TEST MIXED this week: AMZN (entered Aug 4 at +15.2% above EMA20) is the clearest confirmation, red two days running (-2.07%->-2.15%, cushion 4.5%). But MSFT (entered Aug 3 at +15.5%) RECOVERED (+1.23%->+2.63%, cushion 8.4%) and CRM (Aug 4, +7.2% ext) gave back all gains to flat (-0.33%, cushion 8.6%). QQQ (entered Aug 5, +3.5% mild extension) deteriorated further, red Day 2 (-1.71%, thinnest-tech cushion 2.6%). Net: extension is not a clean loser on a chop tape -- AMZN/QQQ confirm the thesis, MSFT bucks it. Firm rule stands: treat >~6-8% above-EMA extension as size-DOWN or wait-for-pullback; when it co-occurs with a shallow cross (PDBC), SKIP outright. AMZN and QQQ remain the highest fast-death-cross risks in the book.

STACKED-FLAG entries (shallow cross + extended above EMA + thin liquidity together) -- RESOLVED as a SKIP, not a size-down: PDBC (0.15% cross + ~6.05% extended + thin liq, quarter-unit Jul 24) stopped out -2.40% Day 3. Distinguish from a SINGLE shallow-cross flag (BMY/GIS/CAG), a valid size-DOWN. Rule: one flag -> size down; two or more stacked -> skip. CRM (Aug 4) carried TWO soft flags (0.34% cross + 7.2% extended) but no thin-liq strike; taken via notional cap -- gave back its entire Day-1 green to -0.33% by Day 2, so the two-soft-flag boundary test is now NEUTRAL-to-mildly-negative, not a clear pass. Keep the one-flag-size-down / two-flag-skip rule as is.
